fix.summary:
One commit on top of ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh (8ae752b), all in zendriver/core/connection.py.

(1) cancellation-1: in `_register_handlers`, the `except CancelledError` branch now looks for the cancelled enable in self.mapper. It matches by identity of the cdp generator (`t.__cdp_obj__ is enable`), so a pending manual X.enable with the same method name is not mistaken for it. A written enable stays in the mapper until Chrome answers; one that never left is popped. When the enable never left, the domain is rolled back as before. When it was written, the domain stays enabled, so later sends no longer queue a second enable behind the first, and the dialog can be dismissed again. To close the gap the reviewer flagged, `_expect_enable_response()` puts a stand-in Transaction under the same id. Its done-callback removes the domain from enabled_domains if the browser rejects the enable, or if the stand-in is failed by a close, detach or receive error. Without it, a written enable that Chrome later rejected would stay marked enabled and never be retried.

(2) connection-2, lifecycle-3, connection-3: send() wraps `_register_handlers`, the detached check and `_send_transaction` in try/finally with a `sent` flag.
- (a) If the tx is already done after `_register_handlers` (failed by a receive error, close or detach), send() does not transmit it. It raises that failure through the existing `await tx` path, so ProtocolException still gets its command and params annotation.
- (b) If send() leaves without transmitting (exception, cancellation, detached session, or a failed or cancelled write), the finally block pops the tx from the mapper. It also calls `tx.exception()` if the tx was failed meanwhile, which marks the failure as retrieved.
- (c) `_update_manual_domain` now returns the module it added to manually_enabled_domains. The finally block removes that entry again when the manual X.enable never left. An entry made by an earlier call is kept.

While verifying lifecycle-3 with the reviewer's concurrent-stop probe, I found a second path that the listed windows did not cover. The close fails the pending Browser.close tx while `websocket.send()` is still in progress, and then the write itself raises ConnectionClosed. send() raises the write error, so nobody retrieves the tx's own failure. The `tx.exception()` call above covers it. Before: 4 of 6 runs logged the warning on 3.13. After: 0 of 6.

(3) connection-1: a NamedTuple sentinel `_ReceiveError(exception, pending)`. On an unexpected receive error, the browser listener puts it into each attached session's `_inbox`, carrying the ids that session had in its mapper at that moment. It falls back to `_fail_pending_transactions` when a session has no inbox. When the session's `_receive_message` reaches the sentinel, the replies queued ahead of it have already been dispatched. It then fails only the listed ids still in its mapper and returns None, so listener_loop itself is unchanged. Commands sent after the error, which a revived reader answers, are not affected.

fix.notes:
Residual risks and judgement calls:

1. Semantic change from cancellation-1: a cancelled, written enable that the browser never answers now stays marked enabled indefinitely, until a reply, a close, detach or receive error, or the domain going stale. Real Chrome always answers or the session dies, and the reviewer's stress_domains with the default never-answered rate still reported 0 problems.

2. The stand-in replaces the cancelled tx under the same id. A late rejection of an old enable can remove a domain that was meanwhile re-enabled successfully. The cost is one redundant re-enable on the next send.

3. "Written" means `_send_transaction` returned. If websockets' send() is cancelled after handing the frame to the transport (while draining), the enable is treated as not sent and is re-sent once. This is harmless except in the dialog case, where it could stall once more.

4. Undoing a never-sent manual X.enable removes X from manually_enabled_domains, but does not put X back into enabled_domains when it was auto-enabled before. The next send just re-enables it (redundant enable, no functional loss).

5. The sentinel fails the session ids pending at the time of the error. A reply for one of them that a revived reader routes in later is dropped, the same as before.

6. `_send_oneshot` still has the 'failed meanwhile, then the write fails' window. It is only used by `_prepare_headless` and `_prepare_expert`, and was left out of scope.

7. One-off failure of test_select_with_include_frames_clicks_element_in_cross_site_frame in the first 3.13 full run. I did not capture its traceback. It did not recur in 2 more full runs and 8 targeted loops, and nothing in this diff runs on the normal send path. Every changed branch needs a cancellation, a receive error or a send that never left. Most likely a load flake of the cross-site iframe click.

8. The lifecycle-3 fix went slightly beyond the listed windows: `tx.exception()` in send()'s cleanup covers a close that fails the tx and then its write. The new test test_close_during_a_failing_write_leaves_no_unretrieved_failure reproduces the exact 'Transaction exception was never retrieved' for that case.

9. The main checkout and branch ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh are untouched (still 8ae752b). The worktree is detached at e7d5a85. Scratch scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/followup/U1/.

items.description: cancellation-1 is only fixed when one handler domain is enabled lazily. With handlers in two such domains (for example expect_request's Network plus a console handler's Runtime), _register_handlers enables them recursively. Only the innermost enable is written before the Q2 bound fires. That one is kept as enabled, but the outer one never left, so it is rolled back. The first unbounded Page.handleJavaScriptDialog then re-sends the outer enable and waits behind the dialog forever. Each bounded attempt marks one more domain as written, so recovery takes N bounded attempts. Evidence on real headless Chromium (probes/probe_dialog_recover_multi.py, log,network on 3.13 and runtime,log on 3.10): 'handleJavaScriptDialog HUNG (safety net 8s)', then 'second handleJavaScriptDialog OK'. The fake probe probes/probe_two_domain_dialog.py gives 'dismiss attempt 0: HUNG', and the reviewer's proto/pkg gives the same result, so this is a limit of the prescribed approach, not a regression (base never recovers). Possible follow-up: let Page.handleJavaScriptDialog skip handler registration, or write all pending enables before awaiting any of them.

Not caused by this unit; found while stress-testing it. Q1 race: a receive error on a nested domain enable stops the browser reader after the enclosing send already passed its aopen revival check. The enclosing send then writes its next enable or command with no reader and hangs until some later send revives the reader. This explains the rare 'final send ... failed twice' results from stress.py, which keeps faults on during its final check (1 of about 30 runs on 3.10 seed 2 and 1 on 3.13 seed 6; the 3.13 one was traced to two unrelated injected faults). The deterministic repro probes/probe_write_after_reader_died.py hangs the same way on base 8ae752b and on the fix, on 3.10 and 3.13. With faults off for the final check (probes/stress_clean_end.py), 14 seeds gave 0 problems on both Pythons. Candidate follow-up, as connection-2 suggested: revive the reader in _send_transaction.

No test distinguishes the written-enable lookup by identity (`t.__cdp_obj__ is enable`) from the prototype's lookup by method name. A mutation that matches any pending '*.enable' passes all of test_connection.py on both Pythons. All other mutations were caught: removing the stand-in, tx.exception(), the manual undo, the tx.done() check, the mapper pop or the written check, emptying the sentinel's id list, and failing session commands directly (the last one is caught on 3.13 only, which is expected).

Minor behaviour notes: (1) _update_manual_domain(…, 'disable') still updates the bookkeeping before the disable is sent. With fix (a), an X.disable that failed meanwhile is no longer sent, but X has already been dropped from both lists. At worst X is re-enabled redundantly. (2) If two manual X.enable() calls run at once and the call that added the entry is cancelled, it removes the entry even though the other call sent X.enable. At worst X is auto-enabled redundantly. (3) _update_manual_domain is annotated `-> Any`; `ModuleType | None` would say more.

fix.summary: Fixed cancellation-2. In zendriver/core/tab.py, a new private helper `_wait_for(aw, timeout)` built on asyncio.wait replaces the four Q2 asyncio.wait_for bounds: _poll_with_timeout (used by find, select, find_all, select_all, wait_for and Tab.__call__), Tab.xpath, and in zendriver/core/cloudflare.py cf_wait_for_interactive_challenge and the verify_cf click phase. The helper runs the attempt with ensure_future and waits on it with asyncio.wait({task}, timeout). If the caller is cancelled, it cancels the attempt, waits for it to finish and re-raises the CancelledError, even when the attempt finished in the same loop iteration (CPython gh-86296). On timeout it cancels the attempt, waits for it and raises asyncio.TimeoutError, or the attempt's own non-cancel exception, as wait_for does. A done callback reads the attempt's result so asyncio never logs 'exception was never retrieved'. The call sites are changed only from asyncio.wait_for to _wait_for, so the TimeoutError messages, xpath's [], cf_is_interactive_challenge_present's False, the one-shot behaviour for timeout <= 0 and the 0.5 s grace stay as they were. Browser._stop, and the wait_for calls that already existed before the bug hunt (Tab.get navigate, wait_for_ready_state, line ~1169), were left alone. There are no public signature changes and the patch is one commit on top of 8ae752b. HEAD is now detached.

fix.notes:
Residual risks and behaviour notes:
(1) On Python 3.12 and later, the helper now runs the attempt in its own task, where wait_for ran it inline. As a result, when the caller is cancelled and the attempt's cleanup raises a different exception, the caller now gets CancelledError instead of that exception. That matches what 3.10/3.11 wait_for already did, and it is what a canceller expects. The error is also retrieved, so nothing is logged.
(2) If the bound runs out and the attempt swallows its cancellation and returns a value, the helper raises TimeoutError. 3.10 wait_for does the same; 3.12+ wait_for returned the value. If the attempt instead raises a non-cancel exception while it is being cancelled, that exception propagates, the same as wait_for on every version.
(3) As with wait_for, the helper waits for the cancelled attempt to finish. An attempt that ignores its cancellation would therefore still block the caller. This is unchanged.
(4) Out of scope and unchanged: three asyncio.wait_for calls that existed before the bug hunt keep the gh-86296 window on 3.10/3.11. They are Tab.wait_for_ready_state (line ~1450), Tab.get's navigate bound (~599) and the bound at ~1169. Browser._stop's wait_for was left alone as instructed. Converting them to _wait_for would be a one-word change if wanted later.
(5) The cancellation-1 wedge (Q2 timeout plus Q12 rollback behind a dialog) is a separate finding and is not addressed here.
(6) The new tests are deterministic: the answer future is resolved and task.cancel() is called in the same loop iteration, and every wait has a positive outer safety-net timeout. The retrieval test filters caplog on a unique message ('the cancelled attempt failed'), so unrelated 'never retrieved' logs from other tests cannot make it fail.
Scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/followup/U2/ (venv313, venv311, probes/, fail_before_310.txt). Nothing was pushed.

items.description: Note (2) in the fixer's report is wrong, and so is the docstring's implied parity with wait_for, in one corner case. When the bound runs out and the attempt swallows its cancellation and returns a value, asyncio.wait_for returns that value on 3.10.20, 3.11.17 and 3.13.16. In 3.10's code this is `try: return fut.result() except CancelledError: raise TimeoutError`. The helper raises asyncio.TimeoutError instead (probe_helper_edges.py case_swallow_then_return). No polling path in zendriver swallows CancelledError: xpath's `except Exception` does not catch it, and Connection._register_handlers re-raises it. So this case cannot happen with current code, and TimeoutError is arguably the better outcome. Only the notes and the docstring wording are off.

Test gap: nothing checks that the caller's CancelledError is raised only after the cancelled attempt has finished. As a mutation, I deleted `await asyncio.wait({task})` from the `except asyncio.CancelledError` branch of _wait_for. All 45 new and Q2 tests in tests/core/test_tab.py and tests/core/test_cloudflare.py still passed on 3.10 and 3.13. The helper does the right thing; it just isn't pinned down. A small test would cover it: an attempt whose cancel cleanup awaits briefly and then sets a flag, and an assertion that the flag is set when the caller sees CancelledError.

Out of scope, kept for the record. Some asyncio.wait_for bounds that existed before the bug hunt still have the gh-86296 window on 3.10/3.11: Tab.wait_for_ready_state (tab.py ~1450), Tab.get's navigate bound (~599), the 10 s bound at ~1169, Connection.wait's idle wait (connection.py:594) and browser.py:458. Each could be switched to _wait_for with a one-word change if that is wanted later. Browser._stop was correctly left alone.

Behaviour changes on 3.12+, where the poll used to run inline inside wait_for and now runs in its own task. All of them are benign or improvements:
(a) The caller is cancelled while the attempt's cleanup raises a different exception: the caller now gets CancelledError instead of that exception.
(b) The answer and the bound's expiry land in the same iteration: the call now returns the answer instead of TimeoutError, as 3.10/3.11 wait_for did.
(c) Context variables set inside the poll are no longer visible to the caller. Zendriver uses none.
Outer asyncio.timeout() and asyncio.wait_for() around a polling call still give TimeoutError, and the task's cancelling() count is back to 0 afterwards (3.11 and 3.13).

review.summary:
Approve. Commit 530989e on fix/followup-timeouts fixes cancellation-2 with no blocking problems.

**The helper.** The new _wait_for in zendriver/core/tab.py replaces the four Q2 asyncio.wait_for bounds: _poll_with_timeout (used by find, select, find_all, select_all, wait_for and Tab.__call__), Tab.xpath, cf_wait_for_interactive_challenge and verify_cf's click phase. Its only awaits are asyncio.wait calls, which never catch CancelledError, so the caller's cancellation cannot be lost.
- On caller cancel, and on timeout, it cancels the attempt and waits for it to finish.
- A done callback retrieves the attempt's exception, so nothing logs "exception was never retrieved".
- The call sites only swap the function name. The TimeoutError messages, xpath's [], cf_is_interactive_challenge_present's False, the one-shot behaviour for timeout <= 0 and the 0.5 s grace are unchanged.
- There are no stray edits: CHANGELOG, docs, zendriver/cdp and Browser._stop are untouched.

**Fail before, pass after.** I restored zendriver/ from ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh and ran the 19 new tests:
- 3.10.20: 18 failed, 1 passed. The pass is failed-xpath, which is expected because xpath catches the attempt's exception itself.
- 3.13.16: only the retrieval test failed, since the race does not exist on 3.12+.

With the fix restored they pass on 3.10, 3.11.17 and 3.13, three runs each on 3.10 and 3.13. Removing the done callback makes the retrieval test fail on both 3.10 and 3.13, so that test really exercises the callback.

**Broader runs.**
- With headless Chromium, test_connection, test_tab, test_browser, test_cloudflare and test_expect gave 150 passed and 2 skipped on 3.10, and 152 passed on 3.13. So the 12 integrated fixes still hold.
- The full suite with -n 4 gave 214 passed and 3 skipped on 3.10, and 216 passed and 1 skipped on 3.13.
- The Q2 tests plus the new tests run under asyncio debug and dev mode with -W error::RuntimeWarning: 45 passed. The only warning was the known ResourceWarning from the browser's Popen stdin pipe.
- scripts/lint.sh exits 0.

**Probes.** The reviewer's probes give the same results on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13:
- probe_cancel_swallow.py: ['cancelled' x5].
- probe_cancel_swallow_loop.py: 'task done: True cancelled: True select attempts after cancel(): 0'.
- probe_inf_timeout.py: returns the element for inf, 1e18 and 10**30.

My own edge-case probe compares the helper with asyncio.wait_for on all three versions: cancel arriving with the answer, a cancel during cleanup that raises, a double cancel, a timeout whose cleanup raises, outer asyncio.timeout and wait_for, the attempt cancelled by someone else, and the answer arriving at the deadline. The helper never loses a cancellation, leaves no tasks behind and logs nothing. Plain wait_for logged "never retrieved" on 3.10/3.11.

A real-Chromium probe cancelled 120 scraping loops at random moments (select, find, find_all, xpath, wait_for) on each of the three versions. Every loop ended cancelled, there were no leftover poll tasks or asyncio error logs, and the tab still worked afterwards.

**Non-blocking items** (details in the item list):
- One corner case (an attempt that swallows its cancellation and returns a value at the deadline) is described wrongly in the fixer's notes.
- No test covers waiting for the cancelled attempt to finish.
- Some bounds that predate the bug hunt are out of scope and still have the 3.10/3.11 window.
- A few benign behaviour changes on 3.12+.

fix.summary:
lifecycle-1: ProxyForwarder.close() now takes the server before its first await (`server, self._server = self._server, None; if server is None: return; ... await server.wait_closed()`). A second close() that runs at the same time, for example from a second Browser.stop(), returns at once. So each forwarder is closed by exactly one call and nothing calls wait_closed() on None any more. Browser._stop is unchanged: forwarders are still closed after the process is gone, each bounded by STOP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT. I chose this over popping forwarders in _stop because a close() cancelled before it starts (wait_for wraps it in a task on Python < 3.12) leaves the forwarder in the list, where a retried stop() still closes it. It also avoids cancelling client tasks twice, which could cut off pipe()'s cleanup.

lifecycle-2: In EXITS_A_WHILE_AFTER_SIGTERM the SIGTERM handler now prints 'terminating'. test_browser_stop_keeps_a_process_started_while_it_ran creates the replacement process before stop(), reads that line with a bound (`asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(process.stdout.readline), 10)`), and only then swaps browser._process. It keeps the same assertions: old process exited, `_process` and `_process_pid` still point to the new process. On Windows, terminate() kills the stub without running the handler, so the test expects EOF (b"") there.

Real-Chromium probe concurrent_stop_proxy_real.py: before the fix, 3.10 gave AttributeError in 2 of 3 runs. After the fix, 3 of 3 runs give results ['None', 'None'] on both 3.10 and 3.13.

fix.notes:
Exactly one commit, 02868a8, on fix/followup-stop on top of ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh (8ae752b). The worktree is now detached and clean. Nothing was pushed, and CHANGELOG.md was not touched (its claim that stop() no longer raises when called twice at once is now true for the proxy case).

Residual risks:
1. A second concurrent stop() now returns while the first is still closing the forwarder (at most STOP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT). Before, it raised. The forwarder's server is already closed and its client tasks cancelled at that point.
2. If close() is cancelled or times out after the swap, it does not wait for wait_closed() again on a retry. The old code cleared the list on timeout anyway.
3. With concurrent stop() calls, one may clear() self._proxy_forwarders while the other is still iterating it. This is harmless: the list iteration just ends, and every forwarder still gets closed exactly once.
4. lifecycle-3 is still present and out of scope: on 3.13 the real-Chromium probe once logged 'Transaction exception was never retrieved' for Browser.close.
5. The rewritten test only fails if the swap happens before stop() takes the process, which the SIGTERM line now prevents. If the loop stalls for 0.4 s or more after SIGTERM, the test still passes but does not exercise the keep-new-process check.
6. The Windows branch of the rewritten test (expects b'' because terminate() kills the stub) is untested here. The new forwarder test kills the stub before stop(), so it does not depend on SIGTERM semantics.

The worktree's local branch name worktree-wf_2c9e79a3-fb2-3 was left unchanged.

items.description: zendriver/core/proxy.py ProxyForwarder.close(): only the first concurrent close() waits. A second close() (and the stop() around it) returns at once, while the first is still in gather(client tasks) / server.wait_closed(). So for a concurrent caller, 'close() returned' no longer means the forwarder's client tasks have finished. With asyncio.run this is harmless, because leftover tasks are cancelled and awaited at shutdown. A sturdier version would keep the in-flight close as a task or future and have later callers await it (shielded). Not needed for lifecycle-1.

tests/core/test_browser.py::test_browser_stop_keeps_a_process_started_while_it_ran no longer fails under any stall: I tried stalls of 0 to 1.0 s after create_task and before the swap on 3.10 and 3.13, and every run passed. But it passes without testing anything if the loop stalls about 0.4 s or more between SIGTERM and the swap, because stop() then sets _process to None before the swap. To make it strict, have the stub's SIGTERM handler wait for a line on stdin instead of time.sleep(0.4), and have the test write that line after swapping _process.

The Windows branch of the rewritten test (expects b'' from readline after terminate()) was never run, and CI runs windows-latest. It needs the stdout pipe to reach EOF once TerminateProcess hits sys.executable. That holds when sys.executable is the real interpreter, or a venv launcher that kills its child through a KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job. If the pipe ever stayed open, the test would fail with TimeoutError after 10 s instead of passing. Low risk, but worth a look on the first Windows CI run.

Nit: in test_concurrent_browser_stop_calls_do_not_raise_with_a_proxy_forwarder, the dead browser.connection (ws://127.0.0.1:1) is only there so that the second stop() gets past the `if not self.connection and not self._process: return` guard. Since connection.closed is True, nothing is ever sent on it. The comment does not say this, so a later cleanup could remove the line and silently stop the test from exercising the race.

Out of scope (lifecycle-3, as the fixer noted): the real-Chromium probe concurrent_stop_proxy_real.py on 3.13 still logged 'Transaction exception was never retrieved' for Browser.close, in 2 of 3 runs. On 3.10 there were none.

review.summary:
Approve. Both findings are fixed, and I found no blocking problem.

lifecycle-1: ProxyForwarder.close() now takes and clears `_server` before its first await, so a second concurrent close() returns instead of calling wait_closed() on None. I checked the concurrent case: when one stop() clears the list while another is iterating it, every forwarder is still closed exactly once. Browser._stop is unchanged, so forwarders are still closed after the process is gone, each bounded by STOP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT. This also makes the existing CHANGELOG entry true.

lifecycle-2: the test now waits for a 'terminating' line printed by the stub's SIGTERM handler before swapping `_process`, so the swap always comes after stop() has taken the old process. Its assertions are unchanged.

Evidence (worktree /home/user/zendriver/.claude/worktrees/wf_2c9e79a3-fb2-6, detached at 02868a8, left clean):
- Fail on base: with zendriver/ checked out from ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh, test_concurrent_browser_stop_calls_do_not_raise_with_a_proxy_forwarder failed 3 of 3 runs on 3.10.20 and 3 of 3 on 3.13.16 with `AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'wait_closed'") != None`.
- Pass on fix: both new tests passed 3 of 3 runs on each Python. They were also clean under `-X dev` with ResourceWarning and PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning turned into errors.
- Mutation: changing `if self._process is process:` to `if True:` makes the rewritten test fail on both Pythons (`assert None is <Popen ...>`), so it still catches what it is meant to.
- Stalls: my probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/followup/U3-review/probes/stall_new_body.py injects stalls of 0 to 1.0 s at two points. All runs passed on 3.10 and 3.13.
- Real Chromium: concurrent_stop_proxy_real.py gave results ['None', 'None'] in 3 of 3 runs on each Python, with the profile removed.
- Direct forwarder race: my probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/followup/U3-review/probes/forwarder_close_race.py runs three concurrent close() calls over live CONNECT tunnels. On base, 2 of the 3 raise AttributeError; on the fix all return None, all clients get EOF and no loop errors are logged.
- Regression check: test_connection, test_tab, test_browser, test_cloudflare, test_expect and test_proxy with -n 4 gave 140 passed, 2 skipped on 3.10. On 3.13 the only failure was test_is_scrolled_to_bottom, a known flaky test. test_browser.py plus test_proxy.py passed 3 of 3 runs per Python (44 passed, 1 skipped on 3.10; 45 passed on 3.13). The full suite with -n 4 gave 196 passed, 3 skipped on 3.10 and 198 passed, 1 skipped on 3.13.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh` passes (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy).
- The commit has no trailers and CHANGELOG.md is untouched.

Non-blocking notes:
- A second concurrent close() or stop() returns before the first has finished waiting on the client tasks.
- The rewritten test can pass without testing anything if the loop stalls about 0.4 s or more after SIGTERM; a stdin handshake would make it strict.
- The Windows branch of the test depends on EOF after terminate() and has not been run.
- The test comment does not say why the dead connection is there.
- lifecycle-3 noise on 3.13 is out of scope and still present.
